verses.english: Linked Discourses 3.25
3. Kosala
The Simile of the Mountain
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho rājānaṁ pasenadiṁ kosalaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: King Pasenadi of Kosala sat to one side, and the Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, mahārāja, āgacchasi divā divassā”ti?
verses.english: “So, great king, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

verses.pali: “Yāni tāni, bhante, raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ issariyamadamattānaṁ kāmagedhapariyuṭṭhitānaṁ janapadatthāvariyappattānaṁ mahantaṁ pathavimaṇḍalaṁ abhivijiya ajjhāvasantānaṁ rājakaraṇīyāni bhavanti, tesu khvāhaṁ, etarahi ussukkamāpanno”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, there are anointed aristocratic kings who are infatuated with authority, and obsessed with greed for sensual pleasures. They have attained stability in the country, occupying a vast conquered territory. Today I have been busy fulfilling the duties of such kings.”
“What do you think, great king?

verses.pali: idha te puriso āgaccheyya puratthimāya disāya saddhāyiko paccayiko.
verses.english: Suppose a trustworthy and dependable man were to come from the east.
He’d approach you and say:

verses.pali: ‘yagghe, mahārāja, jāneyyāsi, ahaṁ āgacchāmi puratthimāya disāya.
verses.english: ‘Please great king, you should know this. I come from the east.

verses.pali: Tatthaddasaṁ mahantaṁ pabbataṁ abbhasamaṁ, sabbe pāṇe nippothento āgacchati.
verses.english: There I saw a huge mountain that reached the clouds. And it was coming this way, crushing all creatures.

verses.pali: Yaṁ te, mahārāja, karaṇīyaṁ, taṁ karohī’ti.
verses.english: So then, great king, do what you must!’

verses.pali: Atha dutiyo puriso āgaccheyya pacchimāya disāya …pe…
verses.english: Then a second trustworthy and dependable man were to come from the west …

verses.pali: atha tatiyo puriso āgaccheyya uttarāya disāya …
verses.english: a third from the north …

verses.pali: atha catuttho puriso āgaccheyya dakkhiṇāya disāya saddhāyiko paccayiko.
verses.english: and a fourth from the south.
He’d approach you and say:

verses.pali: ‘yagghe, mahārāja, jāneyyāsi, ahaṁ āgacchāmi dakkhiṇāya disāya.
verses.english: ‘Please great king, you should know this. I come from the south.

verses.pali: Tatthaddasaṁ mahantaṁ pabbataṁ abbhasamaṁ sabbe pāṇe nippothento āgacchati.
verses.english: There I saw a huge mountain that reached the clouds. And it was coming this way, crushing all creatures.

verses.pali: Yaṁ te, mahārāja, karaṇīyaṁ taṁ karohī’ti.
verses.english: So then, great king, do what you must!’

verses.pali: Evarūpe te, mahārāja, mahati mahabbhaye samuppanne dāruṇe manussakkhaye dullabhe manussatte kimassa karaṇīyan”ti?
verses.english: Should such a dire threat arise—a grim loss of human life, when human birth is so rare—what would you do?”

verses.pali: “Evarūpe me, bhante, mahati mahabbhaye samuppanne dāruṇe manussakkhaye dullabhe manussatte kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya aññatra samacariyāya aññatra kusalakiriyāya aññatra puññakiriyāyā”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, what could I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”

verses.pali: “Ārocemi kho te, mahārāja, paṭivedemi kho te, mahārāja, adhivattati kho taṁ, mahārāja, jarāmaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: “I tell you, great king, I announce to you: old age and death are advancing upon you.

verses.pali: Adhivattamāne ce te, mahārāja, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyan”ti?
verses.english: Since old age and death are advancing upon you, what would you do?”

verses.pali: “Adhivattamāne ca me, bhante, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāya?
verses.english: “Sir, what can I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?

verses.pali: Yāni tāni, bhante, raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ issariyamadamattānaṁ kāmagedhapariyuṭṭhitānaṁ janapadatthāvariyappattānaṁ mahantaṁ pathavimaṇḍalaṁ abhivijiya ajjhāvasantānaṁ hatthiyuddhāni bhavanti;
verses.english: Sir, there are anointed aristocratic kings who are infatuated with authority, and obsessed with greed for sensual pleasures. They have attained stability in the country, occupying a vast conquered territory. Such kings engage in battles of elephants,

verses.pali: tesampi, bhante, hatthiyuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
Yānipi tāni, bhante, raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ …pe…

verses.english: cavalry,
chariots,
or infantry.

verses.pali: tesampi, bhante, pattiyuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
verses.english: But there is no place, no domain for such battles when old age and death are advancing.

verses.pali: Santi kho pana, bhante, imasmiṁ rājakule mantino mahāmattā, ye pahonti āgate paccatthike mantehi bhedayituṁ.
verses.english: In this royal court there are ministers of wise counsel who are capable of dividing an approaching enemy by wise counsel.

verses.pali: Tesampi, bhante, mantayuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
verses.english: But there is no place, no domain for such diplomatic battles when old age and death are advancing.

verses.pali: Saṁvijjati kho pana, bhante, imasmiṁ rājakule pahūtaṁ hiraññasuvaṇṇaṁ bhūmigatañceva vehāsaṭṭhañca, yena mayaṁ pahoma āgate paccatthike dhanena upalāpetuṁ.
verses.english: In this royal court there is abundant gold, both coined and uncoined, stored above and below ground. Using this wealth we can bribe an approaching enemy.

verses.pali: Tesampi, bhante, dhanayuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
verses.english: But there is no place, no domain for such monetary battles when old age and death are advancing.

verses.pali: Adhivattamāne ca me, bhante, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāyā”ti?
verses.english: When old age and death are advancing, what can I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”
“That’s so true, great king! That’s so true!

verses.pali: Adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāyā”ti?
verses.english: When old age and death are advancing, what can you do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Suppose there were vast mountains
of solid rock pressing against the sky
drawing in from all sides
and crushing the four quarters.
So too old age and death
advance upon all living creatures—
aristocrats, brahmins, peasants,
menials, corpse-workers, and scavengers.
They spare nothing.
They crush all beneath them.
There’s nowhere for elephants to take a stand,
nor chariots nor infantry.
They can’t be defeated
by diplomatic battles or by wealth.
That’s why an astute person,
seeing what’s good for themselves,
being wise, would place faith
in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.
Whoever lives by the teaching
in body, speech, and mind,
is praised in this life
and departs to rejoice in heaven.”
The Linked Discourses with the Kosalan are completed.
